wulfenite.e: From German Wulfen + -ite, for Austrian mineralogist Franz X. von Wulfen (1728-1805), named in 1841.

s.d: a yellow to orange or brown mineral used as a molybdenum ore
(uncountable) An orange mineral, lead molybdate, PbMoO₄, found in lead veins.

wurtzite.e: From Wurtz + -ite, for Charles-Adolphe Wurtz, French chemist.

s.d: a brownish-black mineral consisting of zinc sulfide
(uncountable) A dark brown zinc iron sulfide mineral ((Zn,Fe)S), a form of sphalerite.
Of or pertaining to wurtzite crystal structure, a hexagonal crystal system named after the mineral wurtzite.
x: A new family of semiconductors has been synthesized for the first time in the form of wurtzite phase nanocrystals of Cu2ZnAS4−x and CuZn2AS4.

wuss.e: 1976–1981 in US college slang. Perhaps abbreviated from wussy, or blend of wimp and puss. Compare earlier wussy.

s.d: a person who is physically weak and ineffectual
